questions.q: Which order_id in orders.csv is missing a customer_name?
questions.explain: Order 1005 has an empty customer_name field between two commas in the raw CSV.

questions.q: Which order_id in orders.csv has a negative quantity?
questions.explain: Order 1014 has a quantity of -1, which isn't physically meaningful for a shipped order.

questions.q: What does validate_orders() do, as written in this lesson?
options: It fixes every problem it finds automatically
It only reports problems as a list of issue messages, without changing the data
It connects to a database to check for duplicates
questions.explain: Validation and cleaning are kept as separate steps - validate_orders() only detects and reports.

questions.q: Why does clean_orders() flag the missing customer_name instead of dropping that row, but drop the negative-quantity row instead of guessing a fix?
options: There's no real difference - both should always be dropped
A missing name is recoverable with a placeholder, but a negative quantity has no safe value to guess, so the row is removed and logged
Both issues are always ignored to save development time
pandas requires every row to be dropped if any column has an issue
questions.explain: The two problems get different treatment based on whether a safe fix is actually possible.

questions.q: When might raise ValueError be the better choice over silently dropping a bad row?
options: Only when the DataFrame has more than 1000 rows
When the pipeline feeds something where loading incomplete or wrong data downstream is riskier than stopping to force a human to look
questions.explain: For higher-stakes targets like billing, stopping the pipeline can be safer than quietly loading bad data.
